jobs.excerpt: About the CompanyBased in San Diego, California, Eyes On Eyecare is a technology and healthcare information company shaping the future of eyecare.
jobs.description:
About the Company

Based in San Diego, California, Eyes On Eyecare is a technology and healthcare information company shaping the future of eyecare. Through brands like Eyes On Dry Eye, Glance, and npiQ, we deliver web applications, accredited education, and data products to tens of thousands of eyecare professionals. Our mission is to support the people who care for vision with the tools, knowledge, and connections they need to do their best work.

Visionary Medical Education (VME) is our accredited independent medical education partner, delivering continuing education programming for optometrists and ophthalmologists across the United States that is accredited by the Council on Optometric Practitioner Education (COPE) and works with partner organization’s to deliver ACCME accredited education.

About the Role

The Director, Clinical Education is the clinical and scientific backbone of VME's educational programming. You own the educational product end to end, from needs assessment and curriculum architecture through faculty selection, learning design, program execution, and outcomes measurement. You are the reason Medical Affairs teams trust that an accredited grant translates into rigorous, independent, high-quality education.

This role is built for a clinician or clinical educator with deep ophthalmic or optometric expertise who has moved into medical education and wants to build something substantial. You bring strong research and analytical instincts, working fluency across the full clinical landscape of eyecare, and the ability to translate complex science into rigorous, practical education that changes how clinicians think and practice.

You will work closely with the Director, Grant Revenue and Supporter Relations to develop educational concepts that address documented practice gaps. You serve as the scientific and educational lead throughout the program lifecycle, from gap analysis through curriculum delivery and outcomes reporting. Educational content, faculty selection, and learning objectives are determined independently of commercial supporters, and protecting that independence is part of the work.

Key Responsibilities

Educational Strategy and Curriculum Development

  • Lead the design and development of accredited continuing education programming for optometrists and ophthalmologists across the full clinical landscape of eyecare, including anterior segment, cornea and ocular surface, dry eye and meibomian gland disease, glaucoma, retina, refractive, neuro-ophthalmology, pediatrics, and emerging therapeutic areas.
  • Conduct rigorous needs assessments using peer-reviewed literature, survey data, claims data, publication trends, and clinician feedback to identify genuine clinical practice gaps.
  • Develop measurable learning objectives that meet educational design standards and align with ACCME and COPE accreditation requirements.
  • Select and justify educational formats based on identified gaps and audience needs, including live symposia, enduring online modules, hybrid programs, case-based learning, and other delivery models.
  • Translate clinical evidence and emerging science into clear, actionable educational experiences that move learners toward competence and performance change.

Program Design and Educational Materials

  • Lead the design and build of educational assets across program types, including slide decks, faculty briefing documents, case studies, panel and roundtable formats, enduring materials, and live program flow and structure.
  • Set and enforce visual, narrative, and scientific quality standards across all VME educational materials.
  • Partner with content and design teams to ensure that the look, structure, and learner experience of every program reflects the rigor of accredited education.
  • Oversee the development of speaker materials, pre-work, learner guides, post-program resources, and any other materials that support the educational objectives of a given program.

Research and Clinical Evidence

  • Maintain working fluency across the breadth of clinical eyecare and deep expertise in one or more therapeutic areas, with the ability to read, evaluate, and synthesize the primary literature.
  • Lead the scientific underpinning of every VME program by sourcing, vetting, and integrating the strongest available evidence into needs assessments, learning objectives, and content.
  • Track emerging clinical evidence, regulatory developments, and standard of care evolution across major therapeutic areas in eyecare.
  • Translate complex clinical research into rigorous educational design without losing scientific accuracy.

Faculty and Key Opinion Leader Relationships

  • Build and maintain a strong network of key opinion leaders (KOLs) and clinical faculty across optometry and ophthalmology.
  • Identify, vet, and manage faculty for accredited programs in compliance with ACCME and COPE independence standards.
  • Support faculty in developing scientifically rigorous, clinically relevant content that is free of commercial bias.
  • Represent VME at ophthalmic society meetings, including the American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO), the American Optometric Association (AOA), the American Society of Cataract and Refractive Surgery (ASCRS), the Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology (ARVO), and others.

Outcomes Measurement and Reporting

  • Design and implement outcomes measurement strategies up to Levels 4 and 5, including pre and post knowledge assessments, competence measures, and performance change tracking.
  • Collaborate on outcomes data analysis to produce evidence-based reports for supporters and accrediting bodies.
  • Continuously improve evaluation frameworks so that data collection is meaningful, rigorous, and aligned with accreditation requirements.
  • Contribute to the scientific quality and narrative integrity of all educational outcomes reports.

Compliance, Accreditation, and Educational Integrity

  • Serve as the internal expert on COPE accreditation standards for optometric continuing education and ACCME Standards for Integrity and Independence for continuing medical education.
  • Maintain the firewall between educational content development and commercial supporter influence in every aspect of the work.
  • Oversee faculty disclosure management, conflict of interest review, and content independence processes.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with the Director, Grant Revenue and Supporter Relations to develop educational concepts grounded in clinical evidence and aligned with identified practice gaps.
  • Contribute clinical and scientific expertise to grant proposals, including needs assessments, learning objectives, and outcomes frameworks.
  • Collaborate with VME events and technology teams on program delivery and learner experience for accredited programming.
  • Provide clinical review and quality oversight for all accredited educational content.

Who This Role Is For

This role is the right fit if you:

  • Are a clinician or clinical educator who wants to build a credible, rigorous medical education function and is ready to make that the center of your professional life.
  • Read and synthesize primary clinical literature regularly and treat research strength as a core part of the job.
  • Hold deep expertise in one or more therapeutic areas of eyecare and have working fluency across the full clinical landscape.
  • Take real pride in the craft of educational design, including the structure of a program, the quality of a slide deck, and the experience of a learner.
  • Have a strong network of clinical thought leaders and enjoy building and maintaining those relationships.
  • Understand and respect the ACCME and COPE frameworks and view educational independence as a feature of the work.
  • Operate well in an entrepreneurial environment where playbooks, templates, and quality standards are still being built.

Who This Role Is Not For

This role is not the right fit if you:

  • Want to remain primarily in clinical practice with education as a secondary interest.
  • Are uncomfortable working alongside a grant funding function and engaging with industry Medical Affairs teams within the bounds of accredited independence.

The Adjunct Faculty Instructor NAV 101 supports the U.S. Naval Community College (USNCC) by delivering high-quality, fully online asynchronous instruction to enlisted Sailors, Marines, and Coast Guardsmen pursuing college-level education. Faculty members teach Naval Studies and/or General Education courses that strengthen critical thinking, leadership, communication, and operational readiness while supporting the Navy's mission of developing a highly educated and mission-ready force.

USNCC courses are delivered through the Blackboard Learning Management System (LMS) in an 8-week online format. Faculty provide engaging instruction, evaluate student performance, facilitate discussions, and deliver timely, meaningful feedback while maintaining the highest standards of academic excellence and professionalism.

What does a typical day look like for an Adjunct Faculty Instructor?

  • Provide detailed written feedback that promotes student learning and academic success.
  • Monitor student progress throughout the course and proactively identify students who may be at academic risk.

  • Maintain weekly virtual office hours and additional flexible office hours as needed to support student success.
  • Prepare a weekly progress report.
  • Submit all grades and required documentation within prescribed deadlines.
  • Prepare end-of-course reports summarizing student performance and recommendations for course improvements.
  • Participate in faculty meetings and collaborate with Course Leads, Academic Affairs, and Student Services when required.
  • Maintain current knowledge within the assigned discipline through professional development, scholarship, research, or participation in professional organizations.
  • Ensure all instructional materials and supplemental content comply with USNCC academic policies, copyright requirements, and Department of the Navy standards.

What qualifications do you look for?

You might be the professional we’re looking for if you have:

  • Authorization to permanently work in the United States without sponsorship.

  • Experience teaching at the collegiate level, in an online learning environment using Learning Management Systems (Blackboard or similar LMS).
  • Appropriate academic credentials and a record of scholarship/research consistent with the assigned teaching role:
    • Demonstrated expertise in military ethics, philosophy, leadership, law (post JD degree, such as, LLM in military law), U.S. history, and political science.
  • Prior experience teaching introductory courses in law of warfare, international law, military ethics, leadership, organizational behavior, law of the sea and freedom of navigation, and security studies.

  • Demonstrated teaching experience in an online modality for working adults; must include experience teaching one semester-equivalent course specifically in an online higher education environment at an accredited college or university demonstrating strong student and/or peer evaluation.

This will typically include at least 10-15 years of direct field experience, with at least five of those years at a senior leadership level, in the specific course area being taught.

We are extraimpressed by folks with:

jobs.title: Patent Docketing Specialist
jobs.excerpt: Aurora Patents is seeking an experienced patent docketing professional to take primary ownership of our U.
jobs.description:
Aurora Patents is seeking an experienced patent docketing professional to take primary ownership of our U.S. and International patent prosecution docket.

As Aurora's primary docketing professional and authority, you will independently own the integrity, administration, monitoring, and day-to-day operation of the firm's patent prosecution docket. As a core member of our firm’s three-person support team, you will be responsible for the firm's docketing system, processes, controls, integrity, and execution. This is not simply a data-entry, calendaring, or niche specialty position. We are looking for someone who understands patent prosecution well enough to independently review correspondence, identify and calculate deadlines, verify the accuracy of our docket, spot inconsistencies, and make sure nothing falls through the cracks, while helping to shape and evolve a critical part of the safeguards that protect our clients' patent rights.

What we do.

We are a patent boutique that specializes in working with early-stage med device, digital health, software, and life science companies to develop valuable patent portfolios through highly tailored, comprehensive strategies. We scale with our clients' needs and deeply understand the nuances of technology and patent strategy—and how to tie them effectively to business objectives.

Who we are.

We are a fully distributed company with a culture that promotes a high degree of autonomy, work ownership, and quality at every step. You work where, when, and how you want—with others who have a deep passion for technology.

We operate differently from a traditional law firm. Our team is collaborative, highly accessible, and intentionally low on hierarchy. That freedom comes with an expectation of ownership: when something is yours, we expect you to understand it, drive it forward, identify problems before they become problems, and communicate clearly with the people who depend on you.

What you'll do.

Your primary responsibility will be owning the integrity and day-to-day hands-on operation of Aurora's patent prosecution docket, including:

  • Docket Ownership & Deadline Management. Review and analyze incoming and outgoing correspondence relating to U.S., PCT, and foreign patent prosecution; identify, calculate, enter, update, and clear statutory and procedural deadlines; monitor upcoming deadlines; and proactively ensure responsible team members are aware of required actions. Docket and deadline management is in collaboration with BHIP Hills A.I.
  • Correspondence Intake & Triage. Manage the intake and triage of USPTO, WIPO, foreign associate, client, and practitioner correspondence, ensuring information is routed appropriately, docketed accurately, and acted upon in a timely manner.
  • Independent Docket Verification. Review prosecution status and official records using Patent Center, WIPO/PATENTSCOPE, EPO Register, foreign patent office resources, and other appropriate sources to verify bibliographic information, priority claims, application status, and outstanding deadlines.
  • Quality Control & Auditing. Conduct routine quality-control audits of docket entries, deadline calculations, bibliographic information, and matter status. Reconcile the docket against official records and source documents, investigate discrepancies, and drive issues through resolution before they create risk of abandonment or loss of rights.
  • Docket Reporting & Follow-Through. Prepare and maintain useful reports showing upcoming deadlines, outstanding actions, portfolio status, and other information needed by practitioners and management. Follow up when necessary rather than simply generating a report and moving on.
  • Matter Intake & Transfers. Establish and verify docket records for new applications, new clients, and transferred matters, including reconstructing prosecution histories where necessary and independently identifying outstanding obligations and deadlines.
  • Process Ownership & Improvement. Help us continuously improve docketing procedures, checklists, controls, and workflows. If you see a recurring source of risk or inefficiency, we want you to raise it and help us fix it.
  • Patent Portfolio Support. Work closely with our patent practitioners and prosecution paralegals to keep portfolio information accurate and current and help create meaningful portfolio insights for our clients.
  • Procure Signatures. Secure signatures on important filing and patent prosecution documents for the filing paralegal and outside law firms associated with our clients.
  • Patent Application & Prosecution Filings. As needed, prepare and file U.S. and international patent applications and prosecution documents, including formal documents such as declarations, assignments, powers of attorney, petitions, IDSs, and other supporting documents.

Who you are.

You are someone who understands that a reliable patent docket is a risk-management system, not just a calendar. And you’re looking for role ownership at a work home that operates more like a scrappy startup than an oppressive law firm. Ideally, you'll also be a good mix of the following:

  • Experienced Patent Docketing Professional. You have significant experience independently docketing U.S. and international patent prosecution matters. Ideally, you have 4+ years of patent prosecution support experience, including substantial responsibility for docket management.
  • Deadline Expert. You understand how to identify and calculate patent prosecution deadlines from source correspondence rather than relying blindly on automated docketing rules. You know the difference between a reminder and a statutory deadline and understand when extensions are, and are not, available.
  • Prosecution Fluent. You are comfortable with the lifecycle of U.S., PCT, and foreign patent applications and recognize the significance of common prosecution events, including office actions, restriction requirements, notices to file missing parts, allowances, issue fees, continuation/divisional deadlines, PCT national-phase deadlines, priority deadlines, IDS obligations, and related prosecution events.
  • Experienced with Official Patent Systems. You know your way around Patent Center and have experience researching matters using resources such as WIPO/PATENTSCOPE, EPO Register, Global Dossier, and foreign patent office databases.
  • Quality-Control Minded. You don't assume that an entry is correct because someone else entered it. You routinely reconcile information against source documents, recognize when something doesn't look right, investigate discrepancies, and close the loop.
  • Technology Comfortable. Experience with a dedicated IP docketing system is required. AppColl experience is strongly preferred, but we can train an otherwise exceptional docketing professional. Experience with Trello, Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, and modern project-management tools is helpful.
  • An Effective Sleuth. You can locate bibliographic and prosecution information from almost any jurisdiction and aren't stopped by incomplete records, an unfamiliar patent office website, or a matter that arrived without a perfectly organized file.
  • Hyper-Organized, Crisp Communicator. You can manage a large number of concurrent deadlines without losing sight of what matters most and can clearly communicate issues, risks, and required actions to practitioners and other team members.
  • Hungry for Autonomy. You can self-direct, prioritize, follow through, and take personal ownership of results. Prior experience working remotely in a distributed environment is helpful.
  • Proactive. You don't view your responsibility as ending when a deadline is placed on a docket. If something appears stalled, inconsistent, overdue, or at risk, you speak up and help drive it to resolution.
  • Detail-Focused. You have an exceptionally high level of attention to detail and accuracy. Small discrepancies bother you - in a good way.
  • Willing to learn. In a backup capacity, you can learn filing procedures in order to be a support when necessary to meet critical statutory deadlines if there is an overflow of filings or the filing paralegal is unavailable.
  • Highly Collaborative and People-First. You enjoy supporting practitioners, inventors, clients, and fellow paralegals; thrive as part of the solution even when things aren’t perfect (yet!); and take pride in making the entire team more effective.

Opportunity.

This is a fully remote, full-time role with a flexible workweek. The position is salaried for a guaranteed 40 hours per week. Straight-time overtime is paid for any hours above. For the right candidate, we’d also be open to considering a salaried, part-time role.

  • Full-time salary range: $85,000-$100,000
  • Benefits include 401k with match, paid time off, and profit sharing. We do not currently offer medical insurance.

Focus note: We're looking for a dedicated W-2 team member—not someone seeking overflow docketing work or a contract docketing engagement.

Location Note: Some job boards require us to specify a city, but we're fully distributed, so you can work from any reasonably well-Internet-connected location in the U.S.

Salary: $85,000 – $100,000 / year

The ideal candidate will have 3+ years of hands-on experience working in a U.S. dental practice and a strong understanding of dental front-office operations, patient communication, scheduling, insurance verification, pre-authorizations, and dental terminology.

The successful candidate must be comfortable communicating with patients in both English and Spanish and have practical experience working with dental insurance, treatment plans, dental coding, and pre-authorization processes.

  • Schedule, reschedule, and confirm dental appointments.

  • Support dental claims and other insurance-related administrative processes as needed.
  • Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with HIPAA requirements.
  • Provide general administrative and front-desk support to ensure smooth daily dental practice operations.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience as a Dental Receptionist, Dental Front Desk Coordinator, Dental Administrative Assistant, or similar role in a U.S. dental practice.
  • Previous experience working remotely in a dental setting is required.
  • Fluent in English and Spanish, with strong verbal and written communication skills in both languages.
  • Strong knowledge of dental office workflows, terminology, scheduling, and patient coordination.
  • Hands-on dental insurance pre-authorization/pre-determination experience — not just theoretical knowledge.
  • Strong experience with dental insurance verification, including eligibility, benefits, coverage requirements, deductibles, copays, and annual maximums.
  • Working knowledge of dental coding and CDT codes.
  • Understanding of dental procedures, treatment plans, and common dental terminology.
  • Basic understanding of dental X-rays and the ability to identify or understand common types of dental radiographs and terminology.
  • Strong patient service and communication skills.
  • Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities.
  • Proficiency with computers, electronic health/dental records, and dental practice management software.
  • Ability to work independently and maintain productivity in a fully remote environment.
  • HIPAA knowledge or certification is preferred.

Preferred Dental Practice Management Experience

Experience with one or more of the following dental practice management systems is highly preferred:

  • Dentrix / Dentrix Ascend
  • Eaglesoft
  • Open Dental
  • Curve Dental
  • Or other comparable dental practice management systems.

Preferred Additional Experience

  • Dental insurance claims and follow-up.
  • Dental pre-authorizations and pre-determinations.
  • Treatment plan coordination.
  • Dental coding and CDT codes.
  • Understanding of dental X-rays and radiographic terminology.
  • Insurance benefit breakdowns and verification.
  • Patient billing, payment processing, and outstanding balance follow-up.
  • Experience communicating with U.S. dental insurance providers.
  • Previous remote dental practice experience.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a bilingual dental professional with strong front-office experience who can confidently communicate with patients, verify dental insurance benefits, navigate pre-authorization requirements, understand CDT codes and dental terminology, and provide administrative support with minimal supervision.

This is not a general medical receptionist position. Hands-on dental practice experience and practical knowledge of dental insurance processes are essential.

ABOUT VICTORY LIVE
Victory Live is a private equity backed technology company aimed at maximizing distribution and yield for live event ticket inventory. We provide an end-to-end software platform for the live ticketing industry, managing thousands of sports, theater, and live music event tickets on behalf of artists, promoters, teams, venues, and professional resellers. Victory Live’s comprehensive offerings include an established B2B marketplace, along with both a full-service and an automated SaaS platform to handle all elements of the ticket sales lifecycle, from ingestion to sales fulfillment.

THE POSITION
The Sr. Software Engineer on our C# and .NET services is the engine room of our engineering org. You will lead projects from planning through execution, write the code on the hardest pieces, and raise the bar for the engineers around you. You'll also be a force multiplier for AI-assisted development on your team, modeling how to use Claude, Copilot, and agentic workflows to ship faster without compromising quality.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead delivery of more in-depth initiatives from planning through launch in partnership with product and technical leadership, where you own the technical execution.
  • Take on the hard parts. When a .NET service needs a rewrite or a hard data migration, you're the one writing it.
  • Shape architecture. Participate actively in design discussions on our C# services, write design docs, and weigh tradeoffs out loud so the team can learn from your reasoning.
  • Mentor mid-level and junior engineers. Pair, code-review thoughtfully, and help teammates level up their skills, including their AI tooling fluency.
  • Drive process improvements. Spot recurring pain in the team's workflow and propose changes, not just complaints.
  • Push the AI-native bar. Build internal tooling, prompt patterns, and agentic workflows that make the whole team faster, not just yourself.
  • Be a reliable code reviewer on PRs across the team, including outside your immediate project area.
  • Operate cleanly on-call. Know your services in production; lead incident response when needed and write the postmortem.

REQUIREMENTS

  • 5+ years building production software, with strong depth in C# and .NET.
  • Demonstrated ability to make sound architectural decisions in a .NET service and explain tradeoffs clearly in writing.
  • Strong technical depth in backend systems, API design, or distributed services built on .NET.
  • Mentorship experience and a track record of helping teammates grow.
  • Fluent, deliberate use of AI tooling across the full engineering lifecycle (design, code, test, debug, review, docs).

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with RabbitMQ or Kafka, Entity Framework Core at scale, and Azure or AWS cloud services.
  • Experience leading projects in marketplace, ticketing, e-commerce, or two-sided platform environments.
  • Comfort with Datadog, Grafana, Kibana, Airbrake, Sentry, OpsGenie, or comparable production tooling.

WHY VICTORY LIVE

  • You'll build the infrastructure live events run on; millions of tickets, hundreds of venues, many of the largest teams and events in the world.
  • A lean team where decisions move fast and your code reaches real fans, often the same week.
  • Every release has stakes. Every improvement is felt.
  • High expectations, low tolerance for politics, and a culture built on writing well and shipping with care.

OUR VALUES
We build the systems that power live event ticketing, and we hold a high bar for how we do it. Four principles run through everything:

  • Quality of life. Sustainable processes over heroics. Nobody should be a single point of failure, and nobody should be afraid to take a vacation.
  • Quality of code. Clarity over cleverness. If a teammate needs a long explanation to follow your code, it needs simplifying. Tests prove your work; they aren't optional.
  • Protection of production. Every change is reviewed, tested, and observable. We build with monitoring in mind from day one so we find problems before our users do.
  • Shared knowledge. We work across time zones, so we communicate in the open. Questions go in channels, not DMs, and one answer becomes shared knowledge.

ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES
We are an AI-native engineering team. Here is what that looks like in practice:

  • AI-assisted engineering. Every engineer uses Claude, Claude Code, Copilot, and agentic tooling as a routine part of their workflow.
  • Async-first. Most decisions happen in writing through Jira, Confluence, PR descriptions, design docs. We over-communicate on changes and under-communicate on noise.
  • Ownership mindset. Engineers are responsible for what they write and no code reaches production without review. Reviewers are co-owners.
  • Observability is part of "done." If the on-call engineer can't understand a system without reading source, more logging, metrics, and dashboards are needed.
  • Preservation of quality of code and life. We write code that is clean, tested, and maintainable so it serves us well over time, and we build sustainable processes so no one burns out or becomes a single point of failure.
  • Shared knowledge and continued education. We grow as a team by learning from each other through reviews, documentation, and collaboration.

OUR STACK & WAYS OF WORKING

  • C# and .NET power our B2B marketplace, distribution integrations, and partner-facing APIs
  • Web & mobile clients, REST APIs, microservices
  • Frameworks and tools: .NET, ASP.NET Core, Entity Framework Core, xUnit
  • Data: MSSQL Server, Postgres, Redis
  • Cloud & infra: Azure, AWS, RabbitMQ, Kafka, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform
  • AI tooling: Anthropic / Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, in-house agentic workflows
  • Observability: Datadog, Grafana, Elastic/Kibana, OpsGenie
  • Collaboration: Jira, Confluence, GitHub, Slack, Miro
  • Async-first, agile cadences, distributed onshore + offshore teams

BENEFITS & PERKS

  • Comprehensive medical coverage
  • 100% employer-paid dental, vision, life, and disability insurance
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Paid parental leave
  • Paid time off and company holidays
  • Employee wellness and professional development opportunities

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, creed, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, gender expression, Veteran status, or another other characteristic protected by state, local or federal law.

jobs.title: Manager, Resource & Capacity Planning
jobs.excerpt: The Manager of Resource & Capacity Planning owns the hours-and-people picture behind a portfolio of 800+ active and pipeline renewable energy projects.
jobs.description:
The Manager of Resource & Capacity Planning owns the hours-and-people picture behind a portfolio of 800+ active and pipeline renewable energy projects. Every megawatt we help design depends on having the right engineers on the right work at the right time. This role will be instrumental in architecting and implementing the firm's demand-capacity forecast in a dynamic, rapidly changing project environment.

As a trusted resource reporting directly to the Executive Vice President, you will have the responsibility of developing and maintaining resourcing plans and effectively identifying, communicating, and coordinating around scheduling and resourcing conflicts. An effective hire will be able to balance the analytical forecasting responsibilities of the role alongside the soft skills required to coordinate with multidisciplinary stakeholders, including at the executive and senior managerial level. As an employee-owner at a firm built on the mission of designing a cleaner future, your role will play a direct part in enabling projects that move the renewable energy transition forward.

Duties & Responsibilities:

Core Functional Responsibilities

  • Own the rolling demand-capacity forecast across active projects, backlog, and pipeline, refreshed on a published cadence so downstream financial and staffing decisions use current data.
  • Own and maintain the standard work breakdown structure (WBS) and planned hours across portfolios, converting probability-weighted pipeline, project schedules, and cost estimates into capacity demand.
  • Model planned-hours burn and capacity exposure by project, portfolio, discipline, and phase, delivering the hours basis used for labor cost and revenue forecasting.
  • Translate utilization, backlog, and pipeline conversion metrics into hiring indicators and staffing recommendations for leadership.
  • Provide capacity and cost-basis inputs to support proposal pricing decisions made by Client Services.
  • Coordinate with Business Development to determine how prospective projects are weighted and incorporated into the forecast model.
  • Facilitate the weekly resourcing meeting with project management and engineering managers to identify and resolve staffing conflicts in advance.
  • Serve as the intake and routing point for capacity-related requests from across the firm.
  • Escalate unresolved cross-functional resourcing conflicts through the established escalation path.
  • Maintain plan-versus-actuals variance reporting across the portfolio, flagging milestone drift and assignment gaps for correction by the owning team.

Quality, Standards & Compliance

  • Drive schedule and resourcing data quality, flagging WBS non-compliance and assignment gaps for correction by the owning team.
  • Apply the established correction protocol for timesheet and cost estimate discrepancies to maintain data accuracy.
  • Co-own metric definitions for utilization, backlog, and conversion rate with Finance and Business Development under enterprise-level governance.
  • Document the data model, metric definitions, and key assumptions so the forecast can be maintained and used by others.

Collaboration & Communication

  • Present demand-capacity forecasts to executive and senior leadership with clarity and transparency; explain underlying assumptions, respond to questions, and adjust forecasts as new information emerges.
  • Coordinate with Business Development, Finance, Client Services, and engineering leadership to maintain one shared set of pipeline, capacity, and financial data.
  • Report capacity constraints accurately and promptly, including when the findings affect proposals, schedules, or hiring plans.
  • Build alignment across functions without direct authority, raising disagreements with the responsible data owner rather than working around them.

Systems, Data & Reporting

  • Act as the accountable owner for the demand-capacity forecasting system of record and its published metrics.
  • Consolidate inputs from CRM, project management, and timekeeping platforms into a single trusted capacity view.
  • Build and maintain reporting that leadership, Finance, and Client Services can use directly, without maintaining parallel models.
  • Improve forecasting, data, and reporting workflows over time, applying automation and AI tools to reduce manual effort.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Perform essential duties including meeting deliverables and deadlines.
  • Perform additional related duties as assigned or directed.

Experience, Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities:

Required

  • 5–8 years in professional services operations, resource planning, or project operations, ideally in architecture, engineering, construction, or consulting.
  • Demonstrated ownership of a demand-capacity or resource forecast used by leadership to make staffing and hiring decisions.
  • Fluency in professional services economics: fixed-fee versus time-and-materials contract structures, margin math, burn rates, and backlog quality.
  • Strong analytical capability, including advanced Excel, experience building models from incomplete or inconsistent data, and the ability to interpret and validate results.
  • Ability to communicate clearly and persuasively with executives and vice presidents, including presenting unfavorable forecasts and supporting assumptions under scrutiny.
  • Ability to work at both a strategic and a detailed level, moving between WBS-level accuracy and firm-level capacity planning.
  • Demonstrated use of AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, or Copilot to support analysis, automation, or reporting workflows; coding experience is not required.
  • Bachelor's degree in business, engineering, construction management, analytics, or a similar field, or equivalent applicable work experience.
  • Ability to keep US Mountain Time Working Hours (~9 a.m. – 5 p.m., M – F.)

Preferred

  • Experience with professional services automation software (BigTime or similar), project management platforms (Teamwork, Asana, Smartsheet), or CRM systems (HubSpot, Salesforce).
  • Experience with Power BI, Tableau, or Looker.
  • Experience building lightweight automations with AI assistance, such as scripts, API integrations, or data pipelines.
  • RMCP or similar resource management credential is desirable.

Benefits for Full-Time Positions:

  • Participation in Revamp's Employee Ownership ESOP program.
  • Competitive compensation with bonus.
  • Full benefits package including 99% employer-paid health, vision, life, and dental insurance.
  • Medical, dependent care, and commuter FSA.
  • Monthly health and wellness stipend.
  • Attractive vacation, sick, and holiday pay.
  • Paid parental leave.
  • 401(k) savings plan with 100% match up to 6%, vested immediately.
  • Paid volunteer time off and charitable donation matching.

About Revamp:

Founded in 2016, Revamp is the premier engineering design firm focused on large-scale renewable energy projects. We are committed to doing our part in the energy transition and providing a welcoming workplace for talented people ready to make a real difference fighting climate change. You'll serve as the company's internal gem expert and primary decision-maker on stone selection, gem procurement, supplier management, and gem quality — supporting our customer-facing teams on all things related to gems.

You'll be evaluated primarily on your ability to select stones that fit each customer's budget and preferences while meeting our quality standard. Because every project is custom, no two sourcing decisions are identical — you'll exercise significant discretion and independent judgment in evaluating options across our supplier network, weighing quality against cost, and making purchasing and quality decisions that directly impact customers and the business.

Gem sourcing & selection

Purchasing & procurement

  • Make purchasing decisions for center stones and other gems, selecting the stone and supplier within company guidelines.
  • Manage the procurement pipeline from order through delivery and storage, coordinating with suppliers and our in-office team.
  • Identify and resolve procurement issues — delays, out-of-stock items, and reorders for stones that break in setting — and determine when project plans need to be adjusted.

Supplier management

Quality assurance

  • Evaluate stones against our quality standards and determine whether they are acceptable for use in customer projects.
  • Determine the appropriate resolution for gem quality issues — accepting, returning, or replacing a stone — and negotiate remediation with suppliers.
  • Investigate and resolve customer concerns regarding stones, deciding on the appropriate remedy on behalf of the company.

Pricing & continuous improvement

  • Review and update our gem estimates and pricing to ensure they are accurate and cost-competitive, recommending changes to management.
  • Evaluate, recommend, and implement improvements to our sourcing, procurement, and quality processes; update internal gem guidance based on project experience.
  • Advise management on supplier performance, market pricing trends, and recurring gem issues.

Your mission is to turn Beefree’s sales motion into a repeatable, well-coached, well-instrumented revenue system. Beefree has two, distinct product lines: Beefree SDK, an embeddable content creation platform, and RGE Studio, an email production suite under our Really Good Emails brand.

Your primary focus will be Beefree SDK, our most strategic sales-led business. It is a technical, consultative sale into SaaS and other companies, typically involving product, engineering, and commercial stakeholders. Because the SDK becomes embedded in our customers’ products, successful deals require strong discovery, multi-threaded account management, and the ability to build trust around long-term product and business impact.

To succeed, you will need to lead by example and stay close to the work. You will be directly involved in selected strategic opportunities, support the team on complex deals, and use those learnings to improve how we qualify, sell, coach, and scale.

This is not a pure management role. It is also not a senior AE role with a leadership title. We are looking for someone who still loves the game as much as they love developing others. The right person will help grow the business directly, and at the same time build the coaching, standards, and operating rhythm that make the team stronger over time.

Your core responsibilities will be to:

  • Lead and support strategic opportunities, especially for Beefree SDK, helping reps with discovery, deal strategy, stakeholder management, technical buyer alignment, and commercial execution.
  • Coach the team helping them win live deals, not just reviewing them afterwards.
  • Own and improve the playbooks for the sales team:talk tracks, qualification, demo flows, follow-up standards.
  • Make the sales motion more repeatable and scalable across the full opportunity lifecycle.
  • Run a clear operating rhythm for pipeline, forecasting and deal reviews, without over-engineering the process.
  • Build an exceptional partnership with Product and Marketing to sharpen buyer narratives, improve campaign handoffs, and create shared visibility into pipeline health.

How you will work:

  • Lead through direct involvement, not distance. You will stay close enough to customers, prospects, and active deals to develop a deep understanding of what problems they are trying to solve, what other solutions they are considering, and how we best fit in.
  • Support strategic opportunities, helping reps with discovery, demos, stakeholder mapping, technical buyer alignment, follow-up, negotiation, and close plans.
  • Use that exposure to raise the quality of the team’s execution, from discovery and demos to stakeholder mapping, follow-up, negotiation, and close plans.
  • Create clarity around what good looks like, through practical standards, simple processes, useful playbooks, and consistent coaching.
  • Work closely with Product, Ops, and Marketing to identify and prioritise high-intent accounts.
  • Use CRM data, pipeline reviews, win/loss signals, and customer feedback to decide where to focus, what to fix, and what to stop doing.
  • Work closely with Marketing and Product to make sure the sales narrative, enablement material, case studies, and customer feedback loop reflect what buyers actually care about.
  • Bring discipline to planning, forecasting, pipeline quality, and budget allocation, without turning the team into a process-heavy organisation.

What success looks like in the first 6 to 12 months:

  • You have personally won strategic deals and set a standard the team can copy.
  • The New Business pipelines are healthier, better qualified and easier to inspect.
  • Deals have clearer next steps, stakeholder mapping and strategy.
  • The team runs on a consistent coaching and review rhythm.
  • The SDK narrative is sharper for both technical and business buyers.
  • Win/loss learning feeds messaging, targeting and product feedback.
  • Leadership has clearer visibility into pipeline quality and forecast confidence.

What we are looking for:

  • A seller who became a leader and never stopped selling
  • A recent track record of personally closing technical, developer-led or PLG deals. What you have closed lately matters more than years on a CV.
  • SaaS sales leadership experience, ideally in martech, developer tools or technical SaaS.
  • Sharp with CRM data, funnel metrics and pipeline analysis, using data to decide, not just report
  • A genuine coach who builds judgement, not script-followers.
  • Remote leadership capability: clarity, energy and accountability in a distributed team
  • Strong communicator across calls, demos, executive conversations and webinars
  • Fluent in PLG: You know how to read product signals and partner across the organization to build sales-assist motions that support them.
  • Real curiosity in the jobs Beefree’s products get done and an authentic passion for the company’s mission
  • Extra points for experience selling to technical buyers. Comfortable with APIs, embedded software, production versus staging, Model Context Protocol and agentic UX.

About Beefree

At Beefree, our hive buzzes with the spirit of invention, profound curiosity, and a down-to-earth approach. We're not just any SaaS company; we're a place where creativity meets technology to empower businesses, creators, and individuals in digital communications. Our mission? To help ideas take flight through an intuitive, no-code, drag-and-drop builder for designing responsive emails and landing pages online and embedded in hundreds of SaaS applications.

We're a fully remote team that values doing things a bit differently. Embracing transparency, we share our journey's highs and lows with the world. As a software company born in Italy, our diverse team stretches from Europe to the U.S., blending the best of both worlds. Shared values unite our collective from different walks of life with a singular mission: to empower everyone to create impactful digital content.

You can read more about the Beefree story, our values and operating principles, and our unique culture at .

Our Way of Working (WoW) provides the flexibility to work from the office, home, or other locations for limited periods of time.

jobs.description:
Business English Coach, Executive Learners | Contract, Remote, JST Hours

The Role

IMMERSE is a language learning company that helps adults build real-world fluency through live instruction and immersive technology.

We are hiring experienced instructors to deliver 1:1 business English coaching to senior professionals at a global enterprise client. Learners are working executives based in Japan. They are advanced speakers who need their English to hold up under pressure in the situations their roles actually demand: running meetings, presenting to leadership, negotiating, and communicating with US-based counterparts across cultures.

Sessions are 50 minutes, one to one, delivered over Zoom. You work with a small ongoing caseload rather than a rotating queue, so you build a real relationship with each learner over time and see their progress.

You will work from an IMMERSE content library developed around the client organization's leadership framework and the communication demands of their roles. For each learner you select and sequence from that library based on their role and goals, and you create additional material where their needs go beyond it. This is not scripted delivery, and it is not building a program from nothing. Expect to spend real time shaping each learner's path and adjusting it as they go.

The role suits an instructor who works well independently with advanced learners, who can read what a senior professional actually needs and adjust in the moment, and who writes feedback a busy executive will act on.

Compensation

This role pays $45 to $70 per session, based on coaching experience and credentials. The session rate covers the 50-minute session, pre-session review of the learner's history and goals, personalization of the session plan within our framework, and written post-session feedback. Onboarding and calibration are paid separately at $20 per hour. If a learner cancels with less than 8 hours notice or does not attend, you are paid 100% of the session rate. Coaches invoice monthly and are paid within 30 days in USD. This is an independent contractor engagement. You are responsible for your own taxes and for holding valid freelance status in your country of residence.

Schedule Availability

Learners are based in Japan and book during JST business hours. Coaches set their own availability within that window. We are currently prioritizing coaches who anticipate consistent availability for multiple sessions per week during JST business hours. Session volume will vary based on learner demand and coach availability.

Why Coaches Like Working With IMMERSE

  • Preparation and written feedback are paid
  • Work directly with senior, motivated learners in leadership roles
  • A content library to build from, with real latitude to personalize
  • An ongoing relationship with a small caseload rather than a rotating queue
  • Paid onboarding, and full pay when a learner cancels late or does not attend
  • Fully remote, with availability you set within our learners' booking window

What You’ll Do

  • Deliver 1:1 business English coaching sessions with executive learners over Zoom
  • Select and sequence content from our library for each learner, and build supplementary material where their goals require it
  • Work through real professional scenarios relevant to their role, such as meetings, negotiations, presentations, and cross-cultural communication
  • Coach pronunciation, grammar, fluency, and professional writing
  • Write post-session feedback each learner can act on
  • Track progress and adjust each learner's path accordingly
  • Communicate proactively with the instructional team

Required Qualifications

  • Four or more years providing 1:1 business or executive English coaching to working professionals, including building individualized programs for corporate or executive clients
  • Master's degree in TESOL, Applied Linguistics, Education, or Business Communication, or equivalent depth of professional experience. We will seriously consider candidates without a master's who meet the experience bar above
  • Strong command of English pronunciation and of professional writing conventions in business contexts, including experience with formal pronunciation assessment
  • Learners are preparing for communication with US-based counterparts, so this role requires the ability to model General American English pronunciation and idiomatic business usage
  • Available to offer regular session times within JST business hours
  • Comfortable using Zoom and learning new platforms
  • Organized, reliable, and professional

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working with Japanese professional learners
  • Prior experience working in a corporate environment
  • Comfort using AI tools for lesson development and personalization

Apply

If you're an experienced English instructor who enjoys building personalized coaching programs for executive learners, we'd love to hear from you.

jobs.description:
About the Role

You'll join zerohash's growing QA function, working alongside engineers and SDETs. As a QA Engineer, you'll own test planning, functional and exploratory testing, and user acceptance testing (UAT) across zerohash's product stack. This is an opportunity to shape testing practices and quality standards as the team scales, with visibility into every product area and a direct line to release quality.

Responsibilities

  • Test coverage: Design, document, and execute functional and exploratory test cases for API- and SDK-based product flows.
  • Automation testing: Pick up automation work on an ad hoc or on-demand basis, addressing automation tech debt and critical-flow gaps, using tooling and frameworks built by SDETs.
  • Cross-functional planning: Partner with product managers, developers, and SDETs to translate acceptance criteria into concrete test scenarios, and proactively call out coverage gaps and edge cases.
  • Release quality: Own regression testing for your assigned area ahead of each release, and support the team's release-readiness process.
  • UAT: Help formalize and run User Acceptance Testing across product and engineering as zerohash standardizes this process company-wide.
  • Defect management: Log, triage, and track defects with clear repro steps, severity, and expected-vs-actual detail; follow issues through to resolution.
  • Automation collaboration: Flag coverage gaps that need deeper automated testing and route them to developers, who own unit and integration test automation.
  • Environments: Test across dev, cert, and prod environments, and participate in release readiness reviews.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of QA or test engineering experience, ideally in fintech, payments, or another regulated, API-driven environment.
  • Strong grasp of QA process across all phases of the SDLC: test planning, test data setup, execution, defect management, and release sign-off.
  • Strong test case design and exploratory testing instincts; comfortable reading API specs and testing REST/JSON APIs directly (e.g., Postman, cURL).
  • Experience with BDD-style test scenario writing (Gherkin/Cucumber or similar).
  • Comfortable writing and maintaining automated tests (e.g., Playwright, Selenium) for occasional ad hoc work and automation tech debt.
  • Proficiency in at least one programming or scripting language used for test automation (e.g., JavaScript/TypeScript or Python).
  • Working knowledge of SQL for data verification and familiarity with Git-based workflows (GitHub).
  • Experience using Jira and Confluence, or equivalent tools, for test planning, tracking, and documentation.
  • Experience with a test management or UAT tool (e.g., TestRail, Zephyr, or similar).
  • Clear, detailed written communication: bug reports and test plans that others can act on without back-and-forth.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, switching between competing priorities and projects.
  • Comfortable collaborating across time zones with a distributed engineering team.

Preferred

  • Experience testing financial transaction flows: ledgers, settlement, reconciliation, or payments.
  • Exposure to CI/CD pipelines and how automated tests fit into them.
  • Experience working in an Agile/Scrum environment (sprint planning, backlog grooming).

About zerohash

zerohash is the leading crypto and stablecoin infrastructure platform and the operating system for digital money, powering the next generation of financial services. Founded in 2017, zerohash enables banks, brokerages, fintechs, and payment companies to offer crypto trading, stablecoin payments, and tokenized assets without having to build or manage complex blockchain infrastructure on their own.

The zerohash platform supports three core pillars: Trade, Transact, and Tokenize. Through a single integration, customers can launch regulated crypto buy, sell, and custody services; enable 24/7 stablecoin-based funding, payouts, and settlement; and issue and manage tokenized assets with built-in compliance, risk controls, and reporting. By abstracting away technical, regulatory, and operational complexity, zerohash allows partners to treat digital assets as just another financial primitive: fast, programmable, and global.

zerohash is trusted by some of the world’s most recognized financial and consumer brands, including Interactive Brokers, Morgan Stanley, Stripe, Franklin Templeton, BlackRock, DraftKings, Gusto, Worldpay, Kalshi, One Pay, among others. Today, zero infrastructure supports millions of end users across brokerage, wealth, payments, and marketplace platforms globally.

The company is deeply regulated and compliance-first, operating across the U.S. and internationally with licenses and approvals that allow partners to enter crypto and stablecoins with confidence. zerohash has become a trusted partner for enterprises seeking to modernize financial products while meeting the highest standards for security, risk management, and regulatory oversight.

To date, zerohash has raised over $280 million in funding from a mix of leading venture firms and strategic investors, including Morgan Stanley, Interactive Brokers, SoFi, Point72 Ventures, Bain Capital Crypto, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and more.

zerohash has been featured in top-tier media outlets such as Bloomberg, CNBC, The Wall Street Journal, Financial Times, Reuters, Forbes, and CoinDesk, and its leadership team regularly contributes to global conversations on the future of payments, investing, and financial infrastructure.

At zerohash, we're building the infrastructure that makes digital money work securely, compliantly, and at global scale.

The zerohash Culture

All zerohash employees are guided by the following characteristics and core principles:

  • Independence/Ownership - An ability to work autonomously. Join zerohash, pitch ideas, and shape the work you do.
  • Passion - We are innovating quickly and challenging the status quo. We want you to think big, be creative and ​make a difference every day.
  • Collaborative - A good attitude and respect for others. We’re teammates, not co-workers. Everything we do is a shared success and equally a shared failure - we talk in terms of “we” not “me”.
  • Initiative - An ability and passion for learning and asking questions. We will champion you, challenge you and push you to achieve your best - and we expect you to do the same.
  • Empathy - An ability to listen, respect, and understand your co-workers, customers, and everyone you interact with no matter how different they are to you.
  • Adaptability - An ability to respond quickly. We are in a fast-paced industry and so we expect you to be creative when solving a new problem and comfortable under pressure.
  • Transparency - We believe that transparency is critical to empowering everyone to make the best decisions, both the company to its people and vice versa.
  • Integrity - Integrity creates trust. As both an organization collectively and as individuals, it is our most valuable asset.

jobs.excerpt: Maybe you call yourself an Internal Communications Manager, a Content Strategist, a Wordsmith-for-Hire, a Chief "Let-Me-Just-Rewrite-That"… or maybe you just call yourself Alex.
jobs.description:
Maybe you call yourself an Internal Communications Manager, a Content Strategist, a Wordsmith-for-Hire, a Chief "Let-Me-Just-Rewrite-That"… or maybe you just call yourself Alex. Whatever title you use, you're the person who takes a messy, half-formed brief and turns it into something people actually want to read, watch, or click through.

What you get

  • €68,000–€78,000 gross per year, based on your experience.
  • €5,000 a year for your own growth, with a real say in how you spend it.
  • 25 vacation days + the option to buy up to 10 more + local public holidays + the option of a sabbatical up to 4 months.
  • Two trips abroad a year with the whole team + occasional drinks and team outings.
  • €500 home-office budget and a great laptop.
  • A well-earned “Hey, well done Buddy!”, now and then.
  • Fully remote, from anywhere in the Netherlands.

Benefits across Europe: the perks above are AYBI’s and go to everyone, everywhere. Statutory benefits (pension, health, social security, leave, sick pay, notice) follow the hire’s country via their local contract or EOR.

About us

All Your BI is a remote-first data agency based in Rotterdam. Since 2019 we’ve grown from a boutique consultancy into an international data team of more than 60 data heroes spread across Europe. We deliver managed BI services for logistics and industrial companies, helping reduce data waste and move businesses forward. We live for the WOW moment, that sparkle in users’ eyes when they gain new insights and discover opportunities. We work according to Holacracy: little hierarchy, lots of ownership. Serious work. Serious fun.

What the job looks like

  • Own our internal communication voice. Company-wide updates, Town Halls and everything in between should sound like All Your BI, not corporate filler.
  • Take a messy, half-formed brief and turn it into a message people actually read: the right words, the right structure, the right length.
  • Build our change muscle by thinking beyond the announcement. What do people need to understand? Where are they likely to get stuck? What actually helps a change land?
  • Own the communication side of change initiatives end to end, building whatever mix of messages, presentations, videos, guides and FAQs the moment calls for.
  • Design and help deliver our Town Halls. Pull together input from across the company, shape the story, build the presentation, prep the presenters, and run the session.
  • Create and coordinate our company-wide communications, keeping our remote, distributed team informed and connected.
  • Keep our People Handbook and other Confluence spaces genuinely easy to use, and help other teams do the same in their own spaces.
  • Take someone else's complex or messy information and turn it into a presentation that's actually clear and easy to follow.
  • Pick the right format for the moment. Sometimes that's a two-minute video, sometimes five slides, sometimes a live session, and sometimes it's deciding we don't need another communication at all.
  • Track how communication is landing and use what you learn to make the next one better.
  • Occasionally help design a learning experience alongside our P&C Lead, and turn a subject-matter expert's know-how into something others can use.
  • Provide some L&D support: keeping tabs on certifications and helping maintain our Udemy setup.

Requirements

What you bring

  • A genuine wordsmith: fluency in English at the level where you catch tone, subtext and register instinctively, not just vocabulary and grammar. You can tighten, restructure, and simplify without losing what the sentence was actually trying to say.
  • Content creation, not just copy: confident building the visual side too — presentations, video edits, and similar — using whatever tools get you there fast, AI included.
  • A good eye: you can spot when something is confusing, too long, visually messy, or unnecessarily corporate, and you know how to fix it.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity: you can take a rough brief, ask the right questions, and build something real without needing everything spelled out first.
  • Ownership: you manage your own pieces of work end to end and get things over the line without much hand-holding.
  • Collaborative: you’ll own a lot, but very little of it will be created in isolation.

We’re a growing team across Europe, and we hire to widen that mix, not narrow it. What matters is what you can do and the perspective you bring, not your age, gender, ethnicity, orientation, disability, background, or where you studied. If the role excites you and you bring most of it, apply: the people who add the most rarely tick every box.

Highlights

You'll turn messy briefs into internal comms and content people actually read: Town Halls, change stories, videos and decks for a remote-first team across Europe.

VyOS Networks is the company behind VyOS, the enterprise-grade open source networking platform for bare metal, cloud, and edge.   • Number of active, transacting partners incorporated into the program.
  • Revenue growth generated through cloud partners and resellers.
  • A repeatable, documented program that scales without proportional headcount.

  • 5+ years in channel sales, partner management, or cloud marketplace roles, with direct experience selling or transacting through AWS, Azure, and GCP marketplaces.

Our Mission

Powering a connected world, engineering for the future.

We believe that the future of networking lies in open collaboration, continuous innovation, and delivering solutions that keep the world connected, efficiently and securely.

We maintain a deep respect for our colleagues, our open-source community, and our clients, ensuring that all interactions are guided by understanding, professionalism, and empathy.
  • Responsibility: Trust is the foundation of our success. We hold ourselves to the highest standards of honesty, dependability, and accountability. Whether delivering on a commitment to a client or collaborating with a team member, we take responsibility for our actions and their impact.

  • Contentment: At VyOS Networks, we believe that work should inspire and fulfill. We create an environment where people are excited to collaborate, share ideas, and find joy in solving real-world problems. We aim to inspire others while finding inspiration in the work we do.

jobs.description:
This is an internal role at Weekday. Not a role by a client.

  • Role type: Full time
  • Location: Remote
  • Working with: CEO and Cofounder

Weekday is an AI-native recruiting platform. We are backed by Y Combinator and Venture Highway (now General Catalyst). We have built the largest white collar talent database in India and have built tools to run outbound recruiting campaigns to them.

About the role

You’ll work closely with the founders on some of the most important problems at the company.

There isn’t a fixed lane for this role. What you work on will depend on what the company needs at the time. That could mean figuring out why a product isn’t growing, launching a new product or market, improving an internal process, working with customers, researching a new opportunity, or taking on a project that simply doesn’t have an obvious owner yet.

This is a hands-on role. We’re not looking for someone whose job ends at analysing a problem and making a recommendation. You should be comfortable getting into the details and doing the work yourself.

As the company grows, the problems you work on will change. We expect the role to change with them.

What you’ll work on

Depending on the week, you might:

  • Take a new idea from a rough hypothesis to something we can actually test
  • Dig into a part of the business that isn’t working well, understand why, and fix it
  • Work on growth for an existing product, including talking to customers, improving positioning, running experiments, or helping close important deals
  • Research a new market, product, partnership, or business opportunity and decide whether it is worth pursuing
  • Build a process or internal tool where none exists today
  • Work with product and engineering to turn customer or business problems into product changes
  • Take ownership of projects that cut across teams and would otherwise fall between the cracks
  • Help the founders make decisions by getting to the underlying facts quickly

Some projects will last a few days. Others may become something you own for months.

What we’re looking for

  • You’re good at figuring things out. You can take a vaguely defined problem, ask the right questions, and get to a useful answer without needing a detailed brief.
  • You’re comfortable doing the work yourself. If something requires talking to customers, going through data, writing copy, building a spreadsheet, or putting together a quick script, you’ll do it.
  • You have good business judgement. You can distinguish between something that is interesting and something that actually matters.
  • You’re comfortable with numbers and technology. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you should be able to work with data and use technology to make yourself more effective.
  • You communicate clearly. You can write well, explain what you’ve learned, and say when something isn’t working.
  • You take ownership. Once you take something on, the founders shouldn’t have to keep checking whether it is moving.
  • You care about details. A lot of this job involves noticing things other people miss and following through on them.
  • You’re comfortable with ambiguity. Priorities will change and you won’t always have a playbook to follow.

We care less about whether you’ve had a “Founder’s Office” title before. You could come from startups, consulting, product, growth, operations, investing, or something else entirely. What matters is whether you can learn quickly and get useful things done.

What you get

You’ll work directly with the founders and get exposure to most parts of the company.

You’ll see how decisions get made, work on problems before they have dedicated teams around them, and have a lot of room to take ownership. If something you start becomes important enough, there’s a good chance you’ll continue to own it.

This role is a good fit for someone who eventually wants to build a company, run a business or product line, or become a generalist operator at an early-stage company.

Company: Coherence OS (United States)
Location: Remote (Global)
Engagement Type: Project-Based (35–45 hours)
Compensation: Cash OR Platform Access (2 Years)

Context for This Role

We are building Coherence OS because we believe the next era of technology requires more than speed and scale — it requires meaning, integrity, and systems that hold over time.

This translation work is part of a broader effort to make advanced systems accessible across languages — not as content, but as infrastructure.

This is not a typical translation project.

You are not translating marketing copy or generic product documentation. You are helping extend access to a system designed to support individuals in navigating and participating in a rapidly changing economic landscape shaped by AI.

The work requires precision, judgment, and respect for meaning. Much of what you will translate involves concepts that must remain structurally intact across languages — not just linguistically accurate, but conceptually faithful.

We are looking for translators who understand that language is not just communication — it is access.

About Coherence OS

Coherence OS is an AI-native operating system focused on preserving human meaning, identity, and ethical coherence in the age of advanced automation.

We are building foundational infrastructure intended to support long-lived, global-scale systems — not short-term SaaS experiments.

This role is for someone who wants to contribute to systems that will matter over time.

Company Stage & Visibility

Coherence OS is in its earliest build phase. We are intentionally operating with a minimal public footprint while core systems, filings, and internal foundations are being finalized.

We have a minimal public website. Full context about the company, mission, and roadmap will be shared during the interview process.

Scope of Work

  • Translate structured system content from English into Vietnamese
  • Preserve meaning, tone, and conceptual integrity — not just literal phrasing
  • Maintain consistency across terminology and frameworks
  • Flag ambiguities or areas requiring clarification
  • Collaborate asynchronously with our internal team when needed

Requirements

  • Native or near-native fluency in Vietnamese
  • Strong proficiency in English (written comprehension required)
  • Ability to translate abstract and conceptual material accurately
  • High attention to detail and consistency
  • Comfortable working independently with minimal oversight

Compensation Options

You may choose between two options:

Option 1: Cash Payment (Project-Based)

  • Fixed, one-time payment upon completion of the translation
  • No ongoing access or involvement beyond the project

Option 2: Platform Access (Preferred Option)

  • 2 years of full platform access (retail value: $4,800+ USD)
  • Access to systems designed to build, operate, and support income-generating activities
  • Removes the need to pay separately for tools, automation, and execution support typically required to run these activities

This option is intended for individuals who think beyond a single project and want access to infrastructure they can continue using over time.

While the retail cost is $4,800+, the actual value is not capped at that number — it depends on how the system is used. Many individuals will spend significantly more than this over time trying to assemble comparable capabilities independently.

Most candidates who recognize the long-term value of access over one-time payment choose Option 2.

Selection Priority

Due to the nature of this work and the role it plays in expanding access globally, priority will be given to candidates who select Platform Access

How to Apply

Please submit:

  • Your CV (in English)
  • A brief note confirming your language pair and availability
  • Which compensation option you prefer

Applications must be submitted in English. Submissions in other languages will not be reviewed.

Closing

This role is best suited for individuals who want to contribute to something being built with long-term intent.

If you are looking for a standard translation task, this will likely feel different.

If you are interested in contributing to systems designed to operate at scale, across languages, and over time — you will likely find this work meaningful.
